newsitem.title: UK: European chemical rationalisation seen continuing.
newsitem.headline: European chemical rationalisation seen continuing.

text.p: The European chemical industry will be forced to rationalise further in the face of increased competition and pressure on profits over the next few years, an industry specialist said on Wednesday.

Philip Leighton of Trichem Consultants told a chemicals conference that sustained profitability would be "harder and harder to achieve" in western Europe, with smaller players being forced to merge or drop out of the business all together.

He also predicted that further investment in Europe would be "very limited," but warned that opportunities for companies to invest in the Middle East and Far East "are fast reducing as incumbent players strengthen their positions."

Leighton told the conference, organised by SMi Ltd, on competitiveness and profitability in the European chemical industry, that western Europe suffered from a combination of high production costs, lower growth in demand than other regions and a poor market structure, with too many players.
He said continued declines in import tariffs would also add to pressure on profits.
Leighton said the industry had responded to pressures by cost-cutting and restructuring, with particular success in polypropolene production.

But he added that the polyethylene industry "remains fragmented and chaotic" despite recent high profile developments such as the joint venture between BASF AG and Shell International Chemicals Ltd announced earlier this month.

Edward Wilson, vice president, strategic development, of the Dow Chemical Co, told the conference that the industry needed to work hard to agree a new regulatory framework for dealing with its impact on the environment.
He said current inconsistency between national rules "is pervasive, leading to inflation of the cost of doing business."
Wilson also called for the creation of a comprehensive feedstock and product pipeline network across Europe.
